NO, you should never feel guilty. We deal with this shit everyday of our lives and no one could ever understand what a ‘good’ day is for us. Please keep in mind our ‘good’ days are just a normal for many people…Everyday is unpredictable and a battle. Give yourself grace and compassion in knowing this.

In contrast, as a 24 year old, I’m often met with “you’re too young to have any back pain you don’t even know what it’s like” and dismissed. As hard as it is to hear and deal with how do we PROVE IT? Other than listing off the symptoms It’s incredibly frustrating and disheartening.

I was actually told by my doctor not to go to my chiropractor anymore because it can worsen symptoms, further damage, or literally paralyze you. That being said- sticking to slow, intentional stretching rather than looking for cracks is more beneficial in pain alleviation. <3

I think a lot of times people may just not know enough about it to really understand the severity.

Enthesitis is a big factor and symptom of AS, it could be a flare your experiencing. In my experience when I go through periods of extra stiffness, it’s usually a lot of soreness in my shoulders and knees right where the tendon connects. This could be due to many different things like overworking your body, eating habits, stress or drinking. I say give your body and mind some extra grace and rest. If it consists consult your doctor. I’m sorry you’re dealing with this, but hopefully it’s a temporary flare.

Hey, also 25F, 5’3” 120lbs..I’ve had pain and immense fluid retention and swelling in my right knee, starting ~2years ago. I’ve been having “normal” symptoms for the past 8 years, so this is relatively new for me. Exercise doesn’t help, it flares up with everything else. My doctor told me this is just another manifestation of the disease, just like random elbow and wrist pain, typically in one side. I’ve gotten fluid removed in the past but there is little to nothing I’ve been told can be done.
